Q2-Q3 quartile means at high rates are substantially above full-run means: AL rate=80: Q2Q3=18.258ms vs full=17.436ms (+4.7%); AL rate=100: Q2Q3=19.192ms vs full=18.434ms (+4.1%). arms.diagnostic_note: Both modes confirm the prediction with R² differences well above 0.02. The formula breakdown is structural: BLIS's nonlinear batch-size terms (sumCtx in tDcKv, MoE nEff scaling) produce sub-linear ITL growth with batch size, making the data concave while the 1/(1-rho) formula is convex. Removing transients amplifies this structural mismatch.

arms.diagnostic_note: The inverted-U shape confirms the ramp-up/drain transient model. AL and AD differ in peak location (80 vs 100) because AD's dedicated decode instances have lower per-instance arrival rate, shifting saturation higher. At rate=150, the system is heavily loaded even during transient phases, compressing the spread relative to the peak.

discrepancy_analysis: All three arms confirmed. Core finding: the formula breakdown is structural, not transient-driven. Removing ramp-up/drain transients (Q2-Q3 analysis) worsens the formula fit (R² drops by 0.044 for AL, 0.023 for AD), because quasi-steady-state ITL is MORE concave than the convex 1/(1-rho) formula. The linear fit consistently outperforms the formula (R²=0.976-0.985 vs 0.919-0.947). The transient effect itself follows an inverted-U pattern peaking at rates 80-100 req/s.
